selected_layer: device_kernel_source::PART_TILES row-address computation (Triton source -> TTIR/BCMLIR index layer)
layer_reason: The only hard failure is an MLIR/Linalg UB overflow at kernel _gqa_fwd_kernel for the two BF16 specializations, and the failed BCMLIR/ttadapter localize the extra live tiles to the runtime tensor divsi/remsi row map that expanded Q loads and Out stores into 128-iteration scalar per-row copies with their own staging buffers. The arithmetic/softmax/PV layers are identical to the previously compiling 047 IR and are not implicated; the host layer (grid/metadata) is already proven by cases 1/2 running. So the smallest layer that can remove the excess buffer without changing tiling or math is this index-computation layer.

host_suggestion.summary: Keep 049 math/host exactly; do not reduce tiling or change arithmetic. Under BLOCK_M%G==0 express e//G = t*(BLOCK_M//G)+lane//G and e%G = lane%G so the runtime tile contribution is a scalar and the lane row/head offsets are compile-time constants; keep direct 2D pointers, all p/sum/PV/normalization arithmetic, tile dims, output layout, cache and partitions. Generic 049 mapping remains as constexpr fallback when G does not divide BLOCK_M. Only this factoring this call; record negative for the next mechanism if no buffer improvement.

selected_repair.name: static lane row/head offsets + scalar tile base in _gqa_tile_part_body
selected_repair.what: Add constexpr STATIC_ROWS = (BLOCK_M % G == 0). When true, hoist lane_seq = offs_e // G and lane_gi = offs_e % G (constexpr arange arithmetic) and their address contributions lane_off_q = lane_seq*q_ss + lane_gi*q_sh and lane_off_o = lane_seq*o_ss + lane_gi*o_sh once outside the grp/t loops; per tile compute only the scalar base seq_base = t*(BLOCK_M//G) and use row_q = seq_base*q_ss + lane_off_q, row_o = seq_base*o_ss + lane_off_o; mask uses seq_row = seq_base + lane_seq. When STATIC_ROWS is false keep the current 049 e//G, e%G mapping verbatim. Addresses, row ownership, mask, and every floating-point expression stay identical.
selected_repair.how_it_targets_failure: Makes the row-offset vector a compile-time constant tensor plus one splatted scalar, the same form that attempt-047's affine offs_m*q_ss had when it lowered to one bulk strided memref.copy for Q and one bulk materialize for Out. Removing tensor divsi/remsi and the runtime per-row address chain is the plausible route to drop the per-row 1x128 staging buffers; one 1x128xf32 buffer (512B) is exactly the reported excess (197120-196608).

tradeoffs.precision: No change. Same rows, same addresses, same qk/p/l_new/PV/out expressions and order; only integer address arithmetic is rewritten by an exact distributive identity guarded by BLOCK_M%G==0. No new cast, no reassociation.
tradeoffs.active_buffers: Expected equal or lower: removes tensor-wide divsi/remsi results and per-row 1x128 address/staging temporaries; lane offset vectors are compile-time constants. Worst case the backend materializes a 128-entry i32 constant vector (512B) and nothing improves.
tradeoffs.handoffs: Unchanged: still 2 matmuls (QK, fp16 PV) and one QK/PV handoff chain per tile, same L0C traffic.
tradeoffs.parallelism: Unchanged: same PART_TILES grid of P=min(20,T), same T tiles, same worker intervals.
tradeoffs.risk: Backend may not fold the constant-vector addptr back into a bulk copy; then UB stays 197120B and compile still fails. In that case record negative and pick an independent buffer-reduction mechanism next call without touching precision.

evidence.finding: Formal four-case feedback on source fd25f87: case1 and case2 (fp16) compile and pass the official checker with unchanged thresholds (mere 9.36e-08 / 8.95e-08, all normal/small/cancel subchecks passed), candidate full_call_us 102.53 / 98.75. case4 and case7 (bf16) fail with MLIRCompilationError at _gqa_fwd_kernel: 'ub overflow, requires 1576960 bits while 1572864 bits available', resource_bytes required=197120 available=196608 (excess 512B); no checker result and no candidate timing exist for those two.

BF16 PART_TILES G=8 128x256 body: %alloc_4 memref<128x128xbf16> is filled by a 128-iteration scf.for that recomputes e_row+i, divsi/remsi by 8 and copies memref<1x128xbf16> per row; the Out path is another 128-iteration scalar loop with tensor.empty tensor<1x128xf32> (512B) + linalg.fill + divf + truncf + materialize per row; v16 is bf16->f32 (tensor<256x128xf32>, 128KB) then f16 (64KB).

Same specialization in TTAdapter form: Q load loop q_34 = 0 to 128 step 1 with divsi(q_36, 8), remsi(q_36, 8), reinterpret_cast memref<1x128xbf16> and memref.copy; output loop likewise per row with a tensor<1x128xf32> temporary, i.e. the dynamic flat row map is the source of the per-row scalar staging tiles carried through UB allocation.

TTIR keeps e_row_32 = addi(splat(t*128), offs_d) : tensor<128xi32>, then arith.divsi and arith.remsi of that whole vector by dense<8>, then two tensor muls to form row_q; no constant folding of lane//G or lane%G occurred, so the lane offsets stay dynamic even though BLOCK_M%G==0.

Compiled attempt-047 BF16 single-chain IR, identical tiling/arithmetic but affine offs_m*q_ss row base: Q loads as one bulk memref.copy from a strided memref<128x128xbf16, strided<[8192,1]>> and Out is one bufferization.materialize_in_destination of the whole 128x128 bf16 tensor. This shows the 512B-class staging buffers are created specifically by the runtime flat row map, not by the matmul/exp2/PV path.

Current source fd25f87 (matches contract feedback); lines 350-358 build seq_row = e_row // G, gi_row = e_row % G and row_q from them per tile, and lines 429-435 reuse them for Out; PART_TILES currently requires BLOCK_M==128, BLOCK_N==256, BLOCK_D==128, SINGLE_KV and BF16, with G=8 in both failing cases.

hypothesis: The BF16 UB peak is pushed over 196608B by per-row scalar staging tiles that the backend creates only because the flat query-head-fast row offsets are computed with runtime tensor divsi/remsi inside the tile loop. Expressed as scalar tile base + compile-time constant lane offsets (exact when BLOCK_M%G==0), the address expression again has the affine/constant-vector form that lowered to bulk strided copies in attempt-047, removing at least one 1x128xf32 (512B) row buffer and permitting compilation within the unchanged 192KB UB budget.

No other line changes: same tl.dot, FP16 rawQK round, exp2 with SM_OFFSET, p16, l_new sum after PV, acc/l_new, mask, stores and host launch.
